question: What is the primary fluid transported within the lymphatic system?
explanation: Lymph is the clear fluid collected from interstitial spaces that travels through the lymphatic vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h1)

question: How does the lymphatic system primarily support the cardiovascular system?

options.A: By regulating the overall resting blood pressure
options.B: By returning leaked interstitial fluid back to the bloodstream
options.C: By pumping oxygenated blood directly to body tissues
options.D: By producing red blood cells to replace old ones

explanation: Fluid constantly escapes blood capillaries into tissues, and the lymphatic system collects and returns this fluid to maintain circulation volume. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h1)

question: What structural feature inside lymphatic vessels prevents the backward flow of lymph?
explanation: Lymphatic vessels contain one-way valves that ensure fluid moves only toward the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h2)

question: A patient asks why walking helps reduce swelling in their legs after surgery. What is the nurse's best response?

options.A: Movement opens up tiny pores in your skin to evaporate excess water
options.B: Skeletal muscle contractions squeeze lymph vessels to push fluid upward
options.C: Walking directly increases the pumping strength of your heart
options.D: Walking prevents blood from entering the lower legs entirely

explanation: Because the lymphatic system lacks a heart, skeletal muscle movement is a primary driver for pushing lymph past internal valves. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is the primary function of lymph nodes?

options.A: Filtering lymph and trapping foreign invaders
options.C: Pumping lymph fluid through the body

explanation: Lymph nodes act as filters that catch bacteria, viruses, and debris before fluid returns to the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h3)

question: Why do lymph nodes often swell up and feel tender when you have an infection?

options.A: White blood cells multiply rapidly inside the node to fight pathogens
options.B: Blood flow to the node temporarily stops completely
options.C: Trapped fluid stretches the outer capsule of the node permanently
options.D: Red blood cells leak out of nearby capillaries into the node

explanation: When germs arrive, your white blood cells throw a massive defense party inside the node, multiplying quickly to fight off the infection. That crowding is what causes the swelling and tenderness!

question: Which lymphoid organ is primarily responsible for filtering blood and destroying old red blood cells?
explanation: The spleen filters blood, recycles iron from hemoglobin, and removes damaged red blood cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the main role of the thymus gland in the human body?

options.A: Regulating blood sugar levels after meals
options.B: Producing bile to help digest dietary fats
options.C: Maturing T-lymphocytes for the immune system
options.D: Filtering bacteria out of swallowed food

explanation: Immature white blood cells travel to the thymus where they develop into functional T-cells capable of fighting infection. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why should you avoid checking blood pressure on the arm of a patient who has had lymph nodes removed from that side?

options.A: It causes immediate permanent damage to the brachial artery
options.B: It can impair fluid drainage and trigger severe lymphedema
options.C: The blood pressure reading will always read falsely high
options.D: It stops white blood cells from maturing in the bone marrow

explanation: When lymph nodes are removed, drainage in that limb is already fragile. Squeezing the arm with a blood pressure cuff can back up fluid and cause a painful swelling condition called lymphedema. Good clinical safety knowledge to keep in mind!

question: A patient has an infected wound on their right hand and notices tender lumps in their right armpit. What does this mean?

options.A: The patient has a primary blood disorder originating in the spleen
options.B: The patient is experiencing normal side effects of red blood cell breakdown
options.C: Bacteria from the hand wound are traveling through lymph vessels to the axillary nodes
options.D: Blockage of the thoracic duct has caused fluid backup in the upper extremity

explanation: Lymph drains from specific regions of the body to nearby nodes. An infection in the hand travels up the arm vessels, causing the armpit (axillary) nodes to trap the germs and swell up.
